summary: In the year 2300, in Lumina—a hyper-technological metropolis where cars fly, intercontinental travel happens in the blink of an eye, and energy seems endless—Leo, a curious 7-year-old boy, is playing with his floating holographic console until the screen flashes red, announcing Low Battery. Annoyed, he heads down to the dusty basement of his old family home in search of spare power cells. Among forgotten boxes and an old photograph of his grandfather dressed as an astronaut, he discovers a metal trunk marked with a faded blue logo that no one recognizes anymore: NASA. Upon opening it, he finds LSR-3000 (Legacy Space Recorder, unit 73LK-L), a sturdy dormant archivist machine that awakens at Leo's touch and unfolds its panels, transforming into a compact space exploration ship. After introducing itself as the guardian built by his grandfather to preserve the memory of the pioneers who never returned home, LSR-3000 reveals that its data banks are corrupted after centuries of inactivity and convinces Leo to climb aboard to embark on a journey through time to the Moon, Mars, and deep space to synchronize live the scientific memories of humanity's forgotten robotic explorers.
details:
We developed an animated graphic novel set in the year 2300, when humanity already lives on Mars. Through Leo, a curious boy, and LSR-3000, an archivist robot built by his astronaut grandfather, the project recovers the history of the NASA machines left behind on the Moon, Mars, and in deep space—such as the Apollo lunar modules, the Ingenuity helicopter, and the Kepler space telescope.

To tackle this challenge, we transformed real historical and scientific NASA data into an immersive narrative that travels to the past to synchronize the memories of these technological pioneers. This project is important because it goes beyond mere technical descriptions to reveal their human and social impact: it shows how each piece of "abandoned" hardware gave rise to everyday technologies—such as microchips, water purification, electric mobility, and autonomous navigation—that drove the development of our society and made inhabiting other worlds possible, ensuring their legacy is never forgotten.
projectRefs: Apollo 15 Astronauts Deploy First Lunar Roving Vehicle
